endorsements.quote: First, physicians and health systems must retain authorship: disable autoaccept and require active review of diagnoses and billing elements.

A clear, nontechnical disclosure that an AI assistant records to help the clinician document the visit —and that the clinician reviews and controls the note—can protect trust without derailing care12.

unlisted_practices: Conduct random audits comparing audio recordings to signed notes to detect drift toward chart-stuffing.
Policymakers and large health systems should require transparency about AI-drafted content and certify ambient scribe tools that meet documentation quality standards.
Evaluate ambient scribe vendor claims against clinical and operational endpoints rather than higher E/M levels or HCC capture.

Health systems should exercise contract and pricing discipline with ambient scribe vendors, including clawbacks if payer offsets occur, data rights protection, avoidance of vendor lock-in, and benchmarking against low-cost scribing.
Clinicians in direct contact with patients should be transparent with patients about AI scribe use.
Payers should audit for medical necessity and, in capitated programs, recalibrate risk models so payments track patients' true need.
Regulators should make downcoding criteria transparent and appealable and set clear rules for AI-generated notes.
Regulators and payers should target audits at truly unjustified upcoding without penalizing documentation completeness.

screen.reason: This is a policy brief discussing the financial and operational implications of ambient AI scribes on coding intensity and outlining governance and policy steps to prevent a coding arms race.
